findings.title: One relationship holds up: new-vehicle units move with total SAAR in the same quarter
findings.text: GPI's same-store new-vehicle unit growth vs total light-vehicle SAAR growth, same quarter: r = +0.93 on levels (n=12) and r = +0.83 on quarter-over-quarter changes (n=11, p = 0.002 after autocorrelation adjustment). Leave-one-out validation confirms real skill (28% lower error than 'same as last quarter'). This is a coincident relationship, not a leading one.

findings.title: As a LEADING indicator (1 quarter ahead) it does not work
findings.text: Last quarter's SAAR vs this quarter's new-unit growth: r = +0.80 looks strong, but the series trend so strongly that the effective sample is ~4 quarters (adjusted p = 0.20), and out-of-sample the lead-1 model beats 'same as last quarter' by only 2%.

findings.title: Used-vehicle units, used GPU and EPS: no indicator shows predictive skill
findings.text: 8 in-sample correlations for used units, used GPU or EPS clear p<0.05 even after the trend adjustment (e.g. gas-price growth vs used-unit growth r = -0.75; change in loan rate vs change in used units r = -0.75), but that is about what chance produces from 280 tests (none survive a multiple-testing correction), and none of the 6 leave-one-out models for used units, used GPU or EPS beat both naive baselines by the 15% margin (0 do). That includes the wholesale index (Manheim). This is the key limitation: the used business is where GPI's recent shortfall sits, and the tracker's indicators cannot yet forecast it.

findings.title: Several very high correlations are trend artefacts
findings.text: E.g. new-vehicle GPU growth vs the Manheim index: r = +0.94, but both series trend steadily over the window, leaving ~4 effective observations (adjusted p = 0.06). Of 280 correlations tested, 48 are nominally significant at 5% versus ~14 expected by pure chance; 17 remain after the autocorrelation adjustment and 4 survive a strict multiple-testing correction.

findings.title: Wholesale/retail spread, ATP, GM: windows too short
findings.text: Retail listing-price history starts 2025 (<=7 quarters), wholesale days' supply and KBB truck ATP only cover 2025-26 (<=4 quarters and 2 quarters), and GM's official delivery tables cannot be fetched automatically. These were not used to build the forecast; any correlation computed on them would be meaningless.

q3_reads.lean: slightly better than Q2 (-2.8%), but inside the error band
q3_reads.basis: Only model with demonstrated skill: same-quarter total SAAR (Q3 SAAR -1.2% YoY, already known) -> -0.9%, +/-4.6 pts (2x leave-one-out error 2.3); it called the direction of the quarter-to-quarter change correctly in 8 of 10 backtested quarters. Coincident, so it is a nowcast, not a forecast, and the band includes Q2's -2.8%.

No indicator model has skill, so the estimate is simply 'same as Q2'. Context only (not validated historically): Cox's retail used sales pace averaged -1.1% YoY in Q3 vs -4.0% in Q2, which would favor some improvement; GPI's shortfall vs the market in Q2 was GPI-specific (sourcing).

q3_reads.lean: flat to modestly better than Q2 (-5.3%)
q3_reads.basis: No model has skill. Seasonal benchmark (Q2->Q3 GPU ratios 2024-25) implies -7.2% to -0.1% (mean -3.6%), helped by an easy comp (Q3'25 GPU was -8.5% YoY). Based on only two prior years.
The best-looking correlations are trend artefacts; no model clears the skill bar.

q3_reads.lean: in line to slight miss vs Street
q3_reads.basis: Not from the indicators (they show no EPS skill). Seasonal benchmark: Q2->Q3 EPS ratios of 2023: 1.029, 2024: 1.010, 2025: 0.907 imply $8.72-$9.89 (mean $9.44) vs vendor Street estimates of $9.88-$10.11, i.e. a required ratio of 1.028-1.052, at or above the top of the historical range. GPI also missed consensus in 4 of the last 6 quarters (4 straight). Offsets: easier GPU comp, wider retail-wholesale spread.

narrative.bottom_line: Honest summary: with 12 quarters of history, the tracker's indicators explain GPI's NEW-vehicle volume in the same quarter (via total SAAR) but show no demonstrated ability to predict used units, used GPU or EPS — the metrics that matter most right now. The Q3 read below is therefore a data-driven lean, not a forecast: new-vehicle units probably a bit better than Q2; used still the weak spot with no reliable edge; EPS more likely in line to slightly below the Street than above it, mainly because the Street's number sits at the top of GPI's own seasonal range and GPI has missed four straight quarters.
narrative.skill_rule: A model may set a frozen central estimate only if its leave-one-out error beats BOTH the 'same as last quarter' and the 'historical mean' baselines by more than 15%. Disclosure: this threshold was fixed after seeing the leave-one-out results (it was raised from 10% to 15% when new-vehicle GPU showed a marginal 11% edge) and before the forecast was frozen — a documented rule, not a strict pre-registration.
